newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ICRC visits "security detainees" in Bahrain.
newsitem.headline: ICRC visits "security detainees" in Bahrain.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has begun visiting detainees held for "security reasons" in Bahrain, an ICRC spokesman said on Friday.

The humanitarian organisation did not yet have a figure for the total number of such prisoners in Bahrain, whom ICRC delegates began interviewing two weeks ago under an accord reached with the government last month.

"The visits are underway," Rolin Wavre, ICRC spokesman in Geneva, told Reuters. "We will give a figure (for the number of detainees) at the end of our visits, but our conclusions will be discussed bilaterally with the authorities."
"The accord we signed with the government of Bahrain on October 28 allows us to visit people being detained for security reasons, in accordance with our standard conditions," he added.
The ICRC's terms include the right to interview detainees in private without witnesses and to make follow-up visits.
At least 27 people have died in political unrest in the Gulf's financial and banking centre since December 1984.

Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ites have waged a violent campaign to demand political and economic reforms, including job opportunities and restoration of an elected parliament dissolved by the government in 1975.
The Sunni-led government says protesters are out to destabilise Bahrain and blames Iran for much of the unrest.
A widespread security crackdown by the government has disheartened the Shi'ite opposition, according to members of the Shi'ite community and Western diplomats in the region.
Influential leaders such as Sheikh Abdul-Amir al-Jamri remain imprisoned along with scores of activists, they add.

Diplomats in Bahrain estimate that the government has rounded up 1,000 political prisoners. Opposition circles give a far higher figure of around 2,500 in jail, but a government official told Reuters they number just a few hundred.
